metadata.title: Political trust among European youth: Evaluating multi-dimensionality and cross-national measurement comparability

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses ICCS 2016 data with a stratified two-stage probability sample design (schools sampled with probability proportional to size; one class in grade 8 randomly selected within each school). For the measurement invariance analyses, the authors explicitly account for the complex nested structure (students nested within schools within countries) and apply a senate weight so that each country contributes equally to invariance estimates (senate weights sum to 500 within each country). This weighting strategy is used to avoid dominance of larger countries in the multi-group invariance testing. Missing data are handled via FIML rather than listwise deletion, so the weighted invariance estimation is combined with a likelihood-based missing-data approach.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible Values are not applicable because the dependent variables are ordinal Likert-scale survey items measuring political trust (six institutional trust items) and the study estimates CFA/MGCFA and alignment optimization for measurement invariance, not cognitive achievement scores with PVs. Missing-data handling is implemented via full information maximum likelihood (FIML), which uses all available information under a likelihood framework rather than PV-based imputation; this is treated here as multiple-imputation-style likelihood-based handling for the schema.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample is drawn from ICCS 2016 and restricted to 15 European countries/regions (Belgium (Flanders), Bulgaria, Croatia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Germany (North Rhine-Westphalia), Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, the Netherlands, Norway, Slovenia, Sweden). ICCS 2016 surveyed approximately 94,000 grade-8 students; the study includes all students in the randomly selected target grade-8 class within sampled schools for the selected countries/regions. The paper reports 52,788 students included and notes 1,014 cases (1.92%) with missing data on all variables; these are excluded from FIML (i.e., FIML uses all available information excluding only cases missing on all variables).

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ICCS 2016 the study leveraged the reported predictors to predict Primary study outcome (heuristic migration), finding that This study uses ICCS 2016 to evaluate the dimensionality and cross-national measurement equivalence of political trust among grade-8 adolescents (about 14 years old) in 15 European countries/regions (N=52,788). Political trust is measured with six ordinal Likert items (trust in parliament, political parties, government, police, armed forces, and courts of justice) and analyzed using CFA for one- vs two-dimensional structures, followed by multi-group CFA (MGCFA) tests of configural and scalar invariance across countries. The two-dimensional model (trust in order institutions vs trust in representative institutions) shows acceptable configural invariance (RMSEA=0.043; CFI=0.997; TLI=0.993) but scalar invariance is rejected (RMSEA=0.074; CFI=0.975; ΔRMSEA=0.029; ΔCFI=-0.020). Because exact scalar invariance is not achieved, the authors use Alignment Optimization to obtain approximate measurement equivalence, finding an average non-invariance of 16.11% (below the 25% threshold) and enabling more defensible cross-country comparisons of latent means. Limitations include reliance on model-fit cutoffs and the fact that approximate invariance tolerates some non-invariance, so theoretical validity of comparisons may be compromised. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: This is not an empirical ML prediction paper: it is a measurement and invariance study using CFA/MGCFA and Alignment Optimization for ordinal survey items. Consequently, there are no ML algorithms, no predictive target variable, and no performance metrics such as accuracy/RMSE/AUC to extract. The schema therefore leaves ml_techniques empty and main_findings as an empty array, while still documenting the ICCS sampling design, weighting strategy, and the reported invariance fit indices.
